question_text:
A 21-year-old woman presents to her primary care physician for evaluation of malaise, joint pains, and rash. She has developed joint pain in her hands over the last month, and has noted a rash over her face that gets worse with sun exposure. She is taking no medication at the present time. On further physical examination, an erythematous rash with a small amount of underlying edema is seen on her face. Her complete blood count is remarkable due to a lymphocytopenia. What are other disorders known to cause lymphocytopenia?
I 22q.11.2 deletion syndrome
II Bruton tyrosine kinase (BTK) defect
III Diphyllobothrium latum infection
IV Whole body radiation
V Glanzmann-Riniker syndrome?

                    ### Question
                    A 21-year-old woman presents to her primary care physician for evaluation of malaise, joint pains, and rash. She has developed joint pain in her hands over the last month, and has noted a rash over her face that gets worse with sun exposure. She is taking no medication at the present time. On further physical examination, an erythematous rash with a small amount of underlying edema is seen on her face. Her complete blood count is remarkable due to a lymphocytopenia. What are other disorders known to cause lymphocytopenia?
I 22q.11.2 deletion syndrome
II Bruton tyrosine kinase (BTK) defect
III Diphyllobothrium latum infection
IV Whole body radiation
V Glanzmann-Riniker syndrome?

                    ### Options
                    opa. I, II, III
opb. I, III, V
opc. III, IV
opd. I, II, IV, V
ope. III, V

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Lymphocytopenia can be caused by several conditions. 22q.11.2 deletion syndrome is associated with immunodeficiency, which can lead to lymphocytopenia due to the underdevelopment of the thymus and subsequent T-cell deficiency. Bruton tyrosine kinase (BTK) defect results in X-linked agammaglobulinemia, leading to immunodeficiency and potential lymphocytopenia due to the absence of mature B cells. Diphyllobothrium latum infection can cause vitamin B12 deficiency, which may lead to hematological abnormalities, including possible lymphocytopenia, though this is less direct. Whole body radiation is known to cause bone marrow suppression, leading to lymphocytopenia. Glanzmann-Riniker syndrome does not have a clear association with lymphocytopenia, and the evidence for this is weak. Therefore, the most consensus-aligned causes of lymphocytopenia among the options are 22q.11.2 deletion syndrome, Bruton tyrosine kinase defect, Diphyllobothrium latum infection, and whole body radiation. The correct option is 'opc. III, IV'.
